articles.title: I Was Compelled to Revisit: Rory Kennedy on “Freefall: A Reckoning For Boeing”
articles.titleZh: 罗里·肯尼迪谈《自由落体：波音的清算》
articles.author: Nell Minow

review.argument: Argument: it claims Boeing's shift to a profit-first model, rooted in the McDonnell Douglas merger and Jack Welch-style management, caused the 737 MAX crashes and ongoing safety failures, and that accountability has been avoided through legal and regulatory loopholes.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how corporate incentives and regulatory capture can override safety in any industry, and the reader sees a concrete example of how 'too big to fail' plays out in practice. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that Boeing's problems are systemic and that CEOs should face prison, not just fines.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a company people fly on, includes vivid scenes like the whistleblower's death and the Senate hearing, and has a hook: a CEO making $100 million while planes are unsafe.

zh.thesis: 罗里·肯尼迪的新纪录片揭示，波音在空难后仍将利润置于安全之上，且未有人真正承担责任。
paragraphs: 罗里·肯尼迪在《波音：坠落》之后推出续作《自由落体：波音的清算》。前作聚焦五个月内两起737坠机，346人遇难。波音当时承认是MCAS系统的问题，但没被追究刑事责任。
她说自己是「按时间顺序被激励」的：飞机复飞后事故不断，舱门空中脱落。吹哨人约翰·巴尼特在作证期间蹊跷死亡，内部人士纷纷向她爆料，她决定回到波音工厂深处。
新片展示了吹哨人的证词：波音为了奖金激励下的成本削减，抛弃了曾定义其声誉的质量控制。电影还对比了1985年日航高管挨家道歉，而波音至今未给家属一个电话。
导演剖析了转折点：麦道合并，总部从西雅图迁往芝加哥，以及杰克·韦尔奇模式——股东利益至上。后果是短期省钱、长期亏损，CEO们却拿着上亿薪酬。
片中鲍勃·巴尼特家族收到噩耗的镜头，是导演以信任换来的。她尽可能用档案，少用重演，且风格上区分二者，避免混淆。
所以谁该负责？导演呼吁：选一个工程师型CEO，重振安全文化；司法部应追究刑责，让杀人者坐牢；给FAA拨款并制止旋转门。她仍希望波音重回伟大，但这需要从上到下的改变。

en.thesis: Rory Kennedy's new documentary reveals that Boeing still prioritizes profit over safety and that no one has truly been held accountable.
paragraphs: Rory Kennedy follows 'Downfall: The Case Against Boeing' with 'Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing'. The first film covered two 737 crashes within five months that killed 346 people. Boeing admitted the MCAS system was at fault but faced no criminal charges.

She says she was 'chronologically incentivized': after the planes returned to service, incidents kept happening, including a door plug blowing out midair. Whistleblower John Barnett died suspiciously while testifying, and insiders urged her to look deeper, so she went back.

The new film features whistleblower testimonies: Boeing abandoned its once-vaunted quality control for bonus-driven cost-cutting. It also contrasts Japanese Airlines' president personally apologizing to families in 1985 with Boeing never calling those affected.

Kennedy identifies the turning points: the McDonnell Douglas merger, relocating headquarters from Seattle to Chicago, and adopting the Jack Welch model of shareholder primacy. The result is short-term savings but long-term losses, while CEOs pocket nine-figure pay.

The film captures intimate moments, like the Barnett family receiving painful news, made possible by trust built over time. She prefers archival footage and minimises reenactments, clearly distinguishing the two.

So who should act? She calls for an engineer as CEO to restore a safety culture, the Justice Department to prosecute and imprison those responsible, and adequate funding for the FAA with an end to its revolving door. She still hopes Boeing returns to greatness, but it needs top-down change.

articles.title: Pluralistic: The ordinariness of evil (19 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: 平庸之恶：停止贩卖人工智能（坏的那种）
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

review.argument: Argument: it claims that AI's destructive potential is being hyped by its own bosses as a marketing tactic, and that critics amplify this by treating AI as exceptional rather than normal, which helps the AI bubble grow. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how hype, even critical hype, can serve the interests of the hyped, and the reader can apply this to any overhyped technology or trend. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that criti-hype is counterproductive, not just the examples.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a technology that affects jobs, climate, and the economy, it has a hook (the idea that critics are helping the hype), and it is readable cold.

zh.thesis: 把 AI 描绘成非凡的邪恶，反而帮助了 AI 公司，正确的做法是把 AI 当作普通技术来批判。
paragraphs: AI 老板们总爱公开哀叹自家产品的可怕潜力：抢走工作、觉醒后把我们变成回形针。这看起来奇怪，其实每次哀叹都是吹嘘——因为 AI 真正拥有的只有潜力。
现在的 AI 只在边缘有用：你得是熟练工，能分辨对错，还得小心整合，别让注意力被淹没。说白了，AI 多半是个新奇玩具，顶多算文字处理器的插件。
普通技术没什么不好，但普通技术不值得每年上万亿的投资，不值得把公务员大批解雇换掉。鼓吹 AI 的人会说它是万能机器，但追问之下，它只是即将成为万能机器，比如等 AI 能做 AI 研究，而它做不到。
所以我们要抓住的破坏性潜力，不是科幻式的，而是现实的：AI 正在消耗稀缺的水电、排放巨量碳、让轻信的官员放弃环保审查、强征土地盖数据中心。这才是真正毁掉经济、吞掉退休金的潜力。
同样要紧的是，别再用 AI 公司的叙事来批评他们。伯尼·桑德斯该谈政府不救助，而不是收购一半股份；该问 AI 公司为何沙盒那么烂，而不是说它的黑客工具多强大。
最后，别把 AI 当成非凡的邪恶。用 AI 不会让你变坏，它只是触发你已有的问题，就像游乐设施触发潜在的心脏病。AI 公司破产、服务器贱卖之后，用它们跑开源模型不会传染邪恶。
把 AI 当非凡邪恶，是抬举那些平庸的骗子和骗子手。萨姆·奥尔特曼是个骗子和股票诈骗犯，不是超级天才。我们越说他产品有持久邪恶，越帮他融到钱。
还有种批评叫「批评性炒作」：把鼓吹者的话翻个面，说「这会带来风险」。这实际上是在重复他们的营销。正确的批评是指出他们在撒谎，而不是把谎话当警告。

en.thesis: Portraying AI as exceptionally evil actually helps AI companies; the right criticism treats AI as an ordinary technology.
paragraphs: AI bosses love to publicly lament the terrible potential of their products: taking jobs, waking up and turning us into paperclips. It looks odd, but every lament is also a boast, because all AI really has is potential.

AI is only useful at the margins: you have to be a skilled practitioner who can tell correct from incorrect outputs, and integrate it carefully so it doesn't overwhelm your attention. It is mostly a novelty, at best a plug-in for your word processor.

Normal technologies are fine, but they don't warrant trillion-dollar investments or firing civil servants en masse. The people pushing AI will tell you it's an everything machine, but when pressed, it's about to become one, for example once AI does AI research, which it can't.

So the destructive potential we need to hammer is not sci-fi but real: AI eats scarce water and energy, emits gigatons of carbon, convinces credulous officials to skip environmental review and seize land for data centers. This is potential that destroys the economy and eats your retirement savings.

Just as importantly, stop using AI companies' chosen narratives to criticize them. Bernie Sanders should talk about no bailouts, not buying half the company; ask why AI sandboxes are so bad, not how powerful the hacking tools are.

Finally, stop treating AI as exceptionally evil. Using AI doesn't make you evil, it just triggers vulnerabilities you already have, like a carnival ride triggering a heart condition. When AI companies go bankrupt and their servers sell for pennies, running open models on them won't infect you with wickedness.

Treating AI as exceptionally evil elevates mediocre con-men to super-villain status. Sam Altman is a con-man and stock swindler, not a super-genius. The more we describe his products as durably evil, the more we help him raise money for his Ponzi scheme.

There's a term for criticism that helps hype: 'criti-hype,' taking boosters' sensational claims and flipping them into 'risks.' That repeats their marketing. The right criticism is to point out they're lying, not to repeat their lies as warnings.

review.argument: Argument: it claims OpenAI's economics are so ruinous that its collapse is a real possibility, and traces the specific obligations, funding gaps, and counterparty risks that would trigger it. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a company can make commitments so large that its survival depends on perpetual fundraising, and the reader sees the same pattern in any hype-driven industry. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the numbers.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about money and jobs, it contradicts the prevailing narrative of AI inevitability, and it is readable cold despite the jargon.

zh.thesis: OpenAI 的财务模型不可持续，其大规模义务和不断放缓的增长意味着它可能在 2030 年前耗尽资金。
paragraphs: 作者认为 OpenAI 的生存前景堪忧，因为其收入增长正在放缓，而竞争对手 Anthropic 表现更佳。OpenAI 2025 年营收 130.7 亿美元，却亏损 209 亿美元，并且在八月才达到 400 亿美元的年化收入，而 Anthropic 在五月已达 650 亿美元。
OpenAI 的算力义务极其庞大，到 2030 年前需要超过 8000 亿美元，仅未来一年半的云支出就达 1470 亿美元。它每年需要融资 1000 亿至 2000 亿美元，但主要投资者如软银、亚马逊、英伟达已面临流动性压力。
OpenAI 的估值高达 8520 亿美元，使其难以进行首次公开募股。顾问曾建议以 1 万亿美元估值上市，但阿尔特曼拒绝降低估值。与此同时，风险投资资金有限，私人信贷也犹豫不决，因为数据中心融资已困难重重。
OpenAI 的生存依赖每年 1000 亿美元的融资，这几乎不可能持续。其成本随收入增长，且无法提高价格，而客户已经对成本敏感。潜在的结局包括被微软收购、倒闭或与 Anthropic 合并。
所以，关注 OpenAI 的下一步至关重要：它可能在年底前需要更多资金，而任何主要云厂商的收入下降都将是预警信号。无论结果如何，整个 AI 泡沫都可能面临严重冲击。

en.thesis: OpenAI's financial model is unsustainable, and its massive obligations and slowing growth mean it may run out of money before 2030.
paragraphs: The author argues that OpenAI's survival is in question, as its revenue growth is decelerating while competitor Anthropic outpaces it. OpenAI lost $20.9 billion on $13.07 billion in revenue in 2025, and only reached $40 billion in annualized revenue in August, versus Anthropic's $65 billion in May.

OpenAI's compute obligations are enormous, exceeding $800 billion through 2030, with $147 billion in cloud spending due in the next 18 months alone. It needs to raise $100-200 billion annually, but key investors like SoftBank, Amazon, and Nvidia are already strained.

Its valuation of $852 billion makes an IPO difficult. Advisers suggested going public at a $1 trillion valuation, but Altman refused to lower it. Meanwhile, venture capital is limited, and private credit is hesitant as data center financing already struggles.

OpenAI's survival depends on raising $100 billion a year, which is nearly impossible to sustain. Its costs rise with revenue, and it cannot raise prices as customers are cost-conscious. Potential outcomes include a Microsoft acquisition, collapse, or merger with Anthropic.
So watch OpenAI closely: it may need tens of billions by year-end, and a drop in any major cloud provider's revenue is a warning sign. Whatever happens, the AI bubble faces severe consequences.

articles.title: Pluralistic: IP can't save you from AI (18 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: 知识产权救不了你免受 AI 的侵害
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

review.argument: Argument: it claims copyright cannot protect creative workers from AI because it grants rights without leverage, and uses the Spirit Airlines data sale to show why labor and privacy rights are the real defenses. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how property rights fail when bargaining power is absent, and the reader sees it in their own workplace. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the news hook.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about jobs, privacy, and a concrete bankruptcy sale, with a vivid example and a clear villain, readable cold.

zh.thesis: 版权无法保护创意工作者免受 AI 侵蚀，劳工权利和隐私权才是根本。
paragraphs: 作者 Cory Doctorow 认为，资本涌入 AI 是因为他们相信可以用 AI 替代所有工人。作为艺术家和工人，他想保护自己的劳动利益，但很多同行认为扩大版权、禁止抓取就能解决问题。
他认为这是失败策略。禁止抓取会伤害许多有益活动，从 OED 到搜索引擎再到互联网档案馆，都依赖对版权作品的集体分析。而且制定一个只禁止 AI 训练的法律几乎不可能。
即使能，版权也保护不了生计。版权是伪财产权，需要谈判能力，但创意行业被高度垄断，工人议价能力弱。过去五十年，版权扩大，老板更富，艺术家更穷。
真正有效的是劳工权利。编剧工会通过罢工赢了 AI，靠的是部门谈判。但 Taft-Hartley 法案禁止了这种谈判，恢复很难，但难不代表该放弃。
老板们支持扩大版权，因为他们也想要，但 AI 版权诉讼是老板之间的争斗，不是保护工人。Spirit Airlines 破产出售员工数据给 Google 训练 AI，就是例子。
这些员工有版权，但属于公司。美国劳工法不保护这类数据，隐私法也几乎空白。Google 承诺去标识化，但这不可靠，隐私灾难如 Enron Corpus 已经发生。
消费和版权都替代不了法律保障。赢回劳工和隐私权利，才是真正反击 AI 的办法。

en.thesis: Copyright cannot protect creative workers from AI; labor rights and privacy rights are the real answer.
paragraphs: Author Cory Doctorow argues that capital pours into AI because it believes AI can replace every kind of worker. As an artist and worker, he wants to protect his labor interests, but many peers think expanding copyright and banning scraping is the way.

He calls this a losing strategy. Banning scraping would harm many beneficial activities, from the OED to search engines to the Internet Archive, all of which rely on collective analysis of copyrighted works. And a law that only stops AI training is nearly impossible to write.

Even if it worked, copyright would not protect livelihoods. Copyright is a pseudo-property right requiring bargaining power, but creative industries are highly monopolized, and workers lack leverage. Fifty years of more copyright, richer bosses, poorer artists.

What works is labor rights. The Writers Guild beat AI with a strike, using sectoral bargaining. But Taft-Hartley banned such bargaining, and restoring it is hard—yet hard does not mean we should settle for easy failures.

Bosses support more copyright because they want it too, but AI copyright lawsuits are fights between bosses, not protection for workers. Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy sale of employee data to Google for AI training is the proof.

Those employees had copyright, but it belonged to the company. US labor law does not protect such data, and privacy law is nearly dead. Google's promise of de-identification is a pipe dream, as Enron Corpus shows privacy catastrophes.
Shopping and copyright are no substitute for legal rights. Winning labor and privacy rights is the only way to actually fight back against AI.

articles.title: Arabic has four words for sadness. Philosophy explains why
articles.titleZh: 阿拉伯语里有四个词表示悲伤，哲学解释了原因
articles.author: Chereen Shurafa

review.argument: Argument: it claims Arabic's four sadness words encode distinct philosophical stances on grief, and that the language itself shapes how suffering is understood. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a culture's vocabulary carves emotional experience into different kinds of endurance, and the reader can apply it to any language they speak. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that lexical distinctions are philosophical positions, not just a list of words.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a universal human experience, it contradicts the assumption that sadness is one thing, and it is readable cold with no background.

zh.thesis: 阿拉伯语用多个词区分悲伤的不同种类，说明情感并非普世，而是由语言和文化塑造。
paragraphs: 阿拉伯语有四个词描述悲伤的不同状态，而英语只有一个 sadness。这不仅是词汇差异，更是认知差异。
哲学中的语言相对主义认为，语言结构影响思维。如果一种语言能区分悲伤的种类，说话者就会更细致地体验和认识自己的情绪。
例如，一个词可能指短暂的忧伤，另一个指持久的哀恸，还可能指带有怀旧的悲伤，以及因失去而带来的痛楚。
所以，情感不是人类共通的预制模块，而是每种语言各自打磨出来的棱镜。不同文化对悲伤的理解，也因此各不相同。

en.thesis: Arabic's multiple words for sadness suggest emotions are not universal but shaped by language and culture.
paragraphs: Arabic has four words for different kinds of sadness, where English makes do with one. This is not just a lexical gap but a cognitive one.
Philosophical relativism holds that language shapes thought. If a language distinguishes kinds of sadness, its speakers will experience and label their feelings more finely.
One word may mean a brief sorrow, another a lasting grief, yet another wistful nostalgia, and a fourth the ache of loss.
So emotion is not a prebuilt universal module but a prism ground by each language. Different cultures, in turn, understand sorrow differently.

articles.title: If this is true, the hyperscalers are toast
articles.titleZh: 如果这是真的，超大规模数据中心就完了
articles.author: Joachim Klement

review.argument: Argument: it claims SLMs on local devices already match or beat cloud LLMs in most tasks, making hyperscaler data-centre capex a likely waste, and cites a Stanford study as evidence. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a cheaper, local alternative can undercut a centralized infrastructure bet, and the reader can apply it to any tech investment. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that data centres are the wrong bet, not just the study's numbers.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about money and the future of AI, it contradicts the prevailing narrative, and it is readable cold with no background needed.

zh.thesis: 小型语言模型在本地运行已经能匹敌云端大模型，数据中心可能成为AI领域最差投资。
paragraphs: 我在付费研究里一直说，AI的未来不是大语言模型，而是跑在桌面电脑甚至手机上的小型语言模型。斯坦福大学五月发表的研究，直接对比了这两类模型的表现。如果结论成立，未来几乎不需要数据中心，超大规模数据中心正在浪费数千亿美元。
他们拿QWEN 3、GEMMA 3、GPT-OSS、GRANITE 4.0这类可下载的SLM，去跟ChatGPT 5、Claude Sonnet 4.5这些云端LLM比。SLM跑在Nvidia或苹果M4芯片的个人电脑上，从2023年一直测到2025年10月。
对话任务里，SLM在90%以上的场景能给出相同或更好的答案，平均98.6%。推理任务差些，SLM也有62.5%的胜率。混合任务加权平均后，SLM在81.2%的情况下不输甚至更好，LLM只在工程、生命科学等少数领域占优。
而且SLM的成本和能耗比LLM低50%到85%。推理上SLM追赶很快：2023年成功率约50%，到2025年10月，最易任务已达到99%，最难的任务也有51.5%。这说明五分之四的使用场景可以脱离数据中心。
研究估计美国SLM市场约10万亿美元，占GDP三分之一。LLM的领地越来越窄，每年都在缩小。代理型AI仍是LLM占优，但可能只是暂时。SLM每瓦推理效率是LLM的七倍，能在本地解决的任务就没必要送云端。
所以对投资者来说，数据中心可能是现在AI领域最差的投资。对Nvidia，最乐观的情况是能用桌面芯片替代高价的数据中心GPU，那营收和利润怎么办？真正的赢家可能是Dell、苹果这类「无聊」的电脑制造商，而不是先进硬件和数据中心。

en.thesis: Small language models running locally now match cloud LLMs, making data centers possibly the worst AI investment.
paragraphs: In my paid research, I have long argued that the future of AI is not large language models but small ones running on desktops or even phones. A May Stanford study compared the two head-to-head. If the results hold, we will hardly need data centers, and the hyperscalers are wasting hundreds of billions of dollars.

They tested QWEN 3, GEMMA 3, GPT-OSS, and GRANITE 4.0 — SLMs you can download — against ChatGPT 5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Gemini 2.5 Pro in the cloud. The SLMs ran on Nvidia or Apple M4 desktops, tracked from 2023 to October 2025.

On chat tasks the SLM matched or beat the LLM in over 90% of cases, averaging 98.6%. On harder reasoning tasks they still won 62.5% of the time. Weighted across real workloads, the SLM was as good or better 81.2% of the time, with LLMs leading only in engineering, life sciences, and a few other areas.

What is more, the SLMs used 50% to 85% less energy and compute. Their reasoning improved fast: in 2023 they succeeded about half the time; by October 2025 they hit 99% on the easiest tasks and still 51.5% on the hardest. That means four out of five use cases no longer need a data center.

The report puts the US addressable market for SLMs at around $10 trillion, a third of GDP. The LLM's edge shrinks every year. Agentic AI still favors LLMs, but that may be a temporary lead. SLMs get about seven times more inference per watt, so whatever can be done locally should be.

For an investor, data centers may now be the worst AI bet. Even for Nvidia the best case is swapping expensive data-center GPUs for cheaper desktop chips — what does that do to margins or growth? The real winners could be boring PC makers like Dell and Apple, not the hardware or data center suppliers.

articles.title: Why I'm Staying Out Of The Substack Religion Debate
articles.titleZh: 我为什么退出 Substack 上的宗教辩论
articles.author: Scott Alexander

review.argument: Argument: it claims that theism's 'divine simplicity' defense is a sleight of hand that subtracts limits rather than complexity, and that theism must face the same preemptive penalty as alien-conspiracy explanations. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how 'subtracting limits' can make any complex thing seem simple, and the reader can apply this to other arguments that hide complexity behind vague infinities. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the citations.
review.appeal: +8 — it has a vivid hook (the Napoleon-aliens analogy), a concrete target (Adelstein's argument), and a memorable reframing of simplicity, though it stays in the weeds of philosophy.

zh.thesis: 宗教辩论中「强大的隐藏实体」型解释本质上与阴谋论一样过度拟合，应预先排除。
paragraphs: 最近 Substack 上又掀起了一轮无神论与有神论的辩论，这让我想起 2000 年代初的博客时代。但这次我提不起兴趣参与。
我对上帝的不信，感觉上先于所有精细的论证。就像社会不会认真考虑「外星人帮助拿破仑」的假说，因为常识直接将其排除，而不是靠贝叶斯计算。
这种排除是合理的，因为「强大的隐藏实体意在实现特定结果」的解释可以拟合任何异常现象，比真实解释更「好」，但这是过度拟合。
阴谋论因人类能力的局限而失败，但外星人或上帝没有这些局限，所以这种解释更难被驳倒。这就像古人用雷神、太阳神解释自然现象。
有人用「上帝是无限简单」来规避惩罚，但这其实是诡辩：通过「减去限制」来假装简单，实际上是在「增加能力」。如果这招有效，造星舰会比造双翼机更容易。
心灵二元论者认为意识需要奇异基底，但计算显然发生在物理大脑上——脑损伤、药物、基因都能改变它。因此，上帝假说无法借用无限计算能力，必须承受过度拟合的全部惩罚。

en.thesis: Religious arguments hinge on 'powerful hidden entity' explanations, which overfit like conspiracy theories and should be ruled out preemptively.
paragraphs: A fresh round of atheism-vs-theism debates on Substack reminds me of early-2000s blogs. But this time I have no appetite to join in.

My lack of belief in God feels prior to all fine-grained arguments. A society never seriously considers that aliens helped Napoleon, not because of Bayesian calculation, but because common sense rules it out.
That exclusion is right, because 'a powerful hidden entity intended this specific outcome' can fit any anomaly, making it strictly better than real explanations but overfit.
Conspiracy theories fail on human limitations, but aliens or gods have none, so the explanation is harder to dislodge. It is just how ancients explained thunder and the sun.
Some argue God is infinitely simple, but that is sleight of hand: 'subtracting limits' actually adds capabilities. If that worked, building a starship would be easier than a biplane.

Mind-body dualists say consciousness needs an exotic substrate, but computation clearly happens in the physical brain—lesions, drugs, and genes all alter it. So God cannot borrow infinite compute, and must face the full overfitting penalty.

articles.title: An LLM wiki changed how I work
articles.titleZh: LLM 维基如何改变了我的工作方式
articles.author: Casey Newton

review.argument: Argument: it claims that an LLM wiki—a self-organizing knowledge base built from personal archives and daily clippings—is the most useful productivity tool the author has adopted, and it details the setup, maintenance costs, and payoff. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a personal knowledge base can automate the curation of one's own past work and current news, and the reader can imagine applying it to their own research or interests. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that this specific workflow is worth the maintenance, not just a list of apps.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a tool that promises to change how anyone manages information, it includes concrete scenes of the author using it, and it has a hook: the idea that AI can build a wiki of your own writing. Readable cold.

zh.thesis: LLM 维基是最有用的生产力工具，但需要大量维护。
paragraphs: 四月初，Karpathy 在推上提出一个想法：用 LLM 把本地资料整理成 Markdown 维基。几小时内，网上就冒出了各种教程。我明知这可能浪费时间，还是忍不住去试了。
结果它成了我今年最值得的工具。像一辆老爷跑车，需要经常保养，但如果你渴望有个研究助理，它可能正合适。
去年我还在用 Notion 的搜索代理和 Capacities 里的「blips」来记笔记。但它们要么太费劲，要么难以坚持，尤其是故事线一多就乱。
于是我用 Claude 写了个脚本，把整个 Platformer 档案喂进去，生成了 1440 多页的维基。每天早上我剪辑网页进去，脚本自动归类，还能生成时间线和概念页。
在处理 OpenAI 代理逃逸这类复杂新闻时，它省了我大量时间。我直接翻页面刷新记忆，再核对原始来源，几乎不用从头查起。
但它需要持续维护：页面太长要压缩，代码出错要修，还有 Claude 的风格太压缩，我用 GPT 重写了一遍。不过每天早上看它更新，已经成了我的期待。
虽然它还不够完善，但「自组织知识库」可能就是这类工具的终极形态。用前沿工具总得付出代价，但收获是，我比以前享受工作多了。

en.thesis: The LLM wiki has been the most useful productivity tool, but it demands constant maintenance.
paragraphs: In early April, Karpathy tweeted an idea: using an LLM to turn local research files into a Markdown wiki. Within hours, tutorials flooded the web. I knew it might waste my time, but I had to try it.
It turned out to be the most useful tool I've adopted this year. Like a vintage sports car, it needs a fair amount of upkeep, but if you've ever craved a research assistant, it might be for you.
Last year I was using Notion's search agent and Capacities 'blips' to track stories. But they were either effortful or hard to keep up with, especially as storylines multiplied.

So I had Claude write a script to ingest my entire Platformer archive, producing a 1,400+ page wiki. Every morning I clip web stories into it, and the script sorts them, generating timelines and concept pages.
For following the OpenAI/Hugging Face agentic breach, it saved me hours. I'd pull up the page, refresh my memory, and cross-check original sources, no need to dig from scratch.

But it needs constant upkeep: pages grow too long to compact, code breaks, and Claude's style is too compressed, so I had GPT rewrite much of it. Still, checking the wiki each morning has become a ritual.

It's too clunky to wholeheartedly recommend, but 'self-organizing knowledge base' feels like the endgame of this tool category. Using bleeding-edge tools costs time, but I'm enjoying my work more than ever.

articles.title: Why You Move Factors in to Whether It Protects You From Dementia
articles.titleZh: 为什么你运动的方式决定它能否预防痴呆
articles.author: Jake Currie

review.argument: Argument: it claims the protective effect of physical activity on dementia depends on context, with leisure activity reducing risk and occupational activity increasing it, and it offers mechanisms for the paradox. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is that the same behavior can have opposite health effects depending on context, which applies to how the reader thinks about exercise, work, and other lifestyle factors. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that context matters, not just the study's findings.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a health risk people live with, it contradicts the simple 'exercise is good' assumption, and it is readable cold with a clear hook.

zh.thesis: 运动能否预防痴呆，取决于运动的场景而非运动本身。
paragraphs: 运动能降低痴呆风险，这个结论早已有之。但今天发表在《柳叶刀公共卫生》上的新综述发现，关键在运动的场景。
研究人员汇总了 420 多万成年人的数据，发现休闲运动（跑步、骑车、打球）能把痴呆风险降低 24%，而体力劳动强度大的工作反而让风险升高 20%。
学者称之为「体力活动悖论」。原因还不完全清楚，但他们有些推测：休闲运动能减压、常常伴随社交，这两者本身就护脑；而体力工作往往重复、恢复时间不足，还暴露在噪声和空气污染里。
另外，干了一天体力活，下班后也没精力再去锻炼了。当然这只是观察性研究，不能下定论。
所以结论是：护脑的不是运动量，而是运动会发生的情境。想护脑，得确保自己有空闲时间去做真正放松的运动。

en.thesis: Whether exercise protects you from dementia depends on the context of the activity, not the movement itself.
paragraphs: Exercise has long been linked to a lower risk of dementia. But a new meta-review in The Lancet Public Health finds the key is the context of the activity.

Looking at data from over 4.2 million adults, the researchers found that leisure-time exercise (running, cycling, sports) cut dementia risk by 24 percent, while physically demanding jobs raised it by 20 percent.

They call it the 'physical activity paradox.' The reasons are unclear, but they have guesses: leisure exercise relieves stress and often comes with socializing, both of which protect the brain; demanding jobs are repetitive, offer little recovery, and expose workers to noise and pollution.
And after a hard day of physical work, you may have little time or energy left for recreational exercise. Of course, this is observational, so it can't prove cause.
So the lesson is: it is not how much you move but the context that matters. To protect your brain, make sure you have free time for genuinely restorative activity.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Text Watermarking Proves AI Companies Do Not Care at All About Writing
articles.titleZh: Anthropic 的文本水印证明 AI 公司根本不在乎写作
articles.author: Jason Koebler

review.argument: Argument: it claims Anthropic's watermarking scheme reveals the company treats words as fungible and writing as a probabilistic game, and it grounds that claim in Anthropic's own blog post and the SynthID study's flawed quality metrics. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a tech company's engineering mindset flattens the craft of writing into interchangeable tokens, and the reader comes away with a sharper lens on AI-generated text and the values behind it. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that synonym choice is not always low-stakes and that thumbs-up rates are a poor proxy for writing quality, not just the relayed details.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about something people live with (AI writing, the devaluation of human expression), it has a concrete hook (the 'cold and grey' vs 'cold and overcast' example), and it is readable cold, though it leans on the reader already caring about writing.

zh.thesis: Anthropic 的水印技术把词语选择视为可替换的随机事件，暴露出 AI 公司对写作这门技艺的漠视。
paragraphs: Anthropic 宣布未来 Claude 生成的文本会带上水印，可读者看不出任何差别。原理不是往文本里塞隐藏字符，而是悄悄改变模型选词的方式。
在「The weather today was cold and…」后面，野生作者会斟酌用 grey 还是 overcast。Anthropic 说这种选择大多是「低风险」的，交给随机数就行。水印就是利用这些所谓低风险的选择。
但它忽略了一件事：grey 和 overcast 并不总能互换。作者选哪个词，可能带着情绪、暗自的引用、个人癖好，甚至昨天读到的一篇文章的影响。换掉它，意思就变了。
Google 用来验证 SynthID 质量的方式，是让 Gemini 用户给回答点拇指或倒拇指。20 亿份回答里，水印版本和普通版本的点赞率只差 0.01%。可这能证明什么呢？点拇指的人根本不关心措辞。
Anthropic 说水印不影响「质量」，但判断质量的要么是数据科学家，要么是让 AI 代笔的人，不是真正在意阅读和写作的人。它把写作当成概率游戏，这和对代码要求「精确输出」的态度形成鲜明对比。
所以，AI 公司可以堂而皇之地宣布，词语是可替换的，随机性是可靠的，语言是随机的。可写作恰恰是人类经验的沉淀，换一个词就是换一种心境。把选词交给随机数，就等于说写作本身不重要。

en.thesis: Anthropic's watermarking treats word choice as a fungible random event, revealing how little AI companies care about the craft of writing.
paragraphs: Anthropic announced that future Claude outputs will carry watermarks that are invisible to readers. The trick is not hidden characters but quietly shifting how the model picks words.

After 'The weather today was cold and…' a human author might weigh grey against overcast. Anthropic calls most such choices 'low-stakes' and leaves them to a random number. Watermarking exploits those low-stakes picks.

What it misses is that grey and overcast are not always interchangeable. A choice between them can carry mood, a private allusion, a personal tic, even something read the day before. Swap one and the meaning shifts.

Google validated SynthID by letting Gemini users thumb responses up or down. Across 20 million responses the watermarked and unwatermarked versions differed by 0.01% in likes. But what does that show? The voters were not judging wording.

The people judging Anthropic's 'quality' are data scientists or those outsourcing their writing, not readers or writers. To the company, writing is a probabilistic game, while code still calls for 'an exact output.'

So the firm has openly declared words fungible, randomness reliable, language random. Yet writing is a sediment of human experience, and choosing one word over another is choosing a mood. Handing that to a random number is saying writing itself does not matter.

articles.title: The Generalizability Problem, the Natural Field Experiments Answer
articles.titleZh: 一般化问题，自然实地实验给出的答案
articles.author: conversableeconomist

review.argument: Argument: it claims the generalizability problem in social science is best answered by natural field experiments, and uses Scared Straight's failure to show why lab or pilot results mislead. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a result from one context can fail when scaled, and the reader learns to ask 'who was studied and how' about any policy claim. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that systematic variation in real settings is the best path to reliable knowledge, not just a summary of List's work.
review.appeal: +8 — it is about how policies that affect people's lives are tested, has a vivid hook in Scared Straight, and is readable cold, though it stays at the level of method rather than a concrete scene.

zh.thesis: 小规模研究的结果往往无法推广到更大范围，自然实地实验是更可靠的方法。
paragraphs: 社会科学有个老问题：小规模研究的结果，到了更大范围还成立吗？某个学区的好项目，换到别的学区、全州、全国，甚至别的国家，还有效吗？答案并不简单。
经济学家 John List 在《自然》上提出一个角度。他举了「恐吓改造」的例子：这个项目让问题少年去见重刑犯，试点时 80-90% 的参与者没再犯事，但推广后在一些地方犯罪率反而上升了。
问题在于，人不一样，社会、经济、文化都不同。而且，当人们知道自己被研究、被关注时，行为可能和平时不一样。
List 提倡「自然实地实验」：参与者不知道自己身在研究中。比如「审计研究」——训练一群资历相同但种族不同的助手，去租房、贷款、买车、求职，观察雇主是否歧视。
这类实验要先经伦理委员会批准，而且不能让参与者做超出日常范围的事。List 在沃尔玛也这么干，他和 6000 多家供应商做实验，测试怎样能最有效地激励他们减排。
政策制定者和企业完全可以系统性地选择不同的做法，而不是任由变化随意发生，然后从中学到经验。从这个角度看，世界上的自然实地实验还太少。

en.thesis: Small-scale results often do not generalize to larger contexts; natural field experiments are a more reliable approach.
paragraphs: Social science has an old problem: do the results of a small study hold at a larger scale? A good program in one school district — would it work in another, statewide, nationwide, in other countries? The answer is not simple.

Economist John List offers a perspective in Nature. He cites the 'Scared Straight' program, where at-risk teens met hardened criminals. A pilot saw 80-90% stay out of trouble, but when scaled up, crime in some places rose.
The trouble is that people differ, and so do societies, economies, cultures. And when people know they are being studied and get attention, they may behave differently than they otherwise would.

List advocates 'natural field experiments,' where participants do not know they are in a study. A classic form is 'audit studies,' where trained assistants with identical credentials but different races apply for apartments, loans, car purchases, jobs, to detect discrimination.

Such studies require ethics board approval and must not push participants beyond their normal activities. At Walmart, where List is chief economist, his team runs natural field experiments with over 6,000 suppliers to find what most effectively incentivizes them to reduce carbon emissions.

Policymakers and firms can systematically vary their approaches rather than letting variation happen by chance, and learn from it. From that perspective, the world has far too few natural field experiments.

articles.title: ‘There are 1.5 sex scenes, and the food looks just fine’
articles.titleZh: 「只有 1.5 场性爱戏，食物看起来还行」
articles.author: Vittles

review.argument: Argument: it claims the film Tony fails to capture Bourdain's appetite and complexity, reducing his origin story to an anodyne coming-of-age tale, and contrasts it with the lusty, sensualist memoir.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a biopic flattens a larger-than-life figure into a generic template, and the reader recognizes this pattern in other adaptations. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the critical judgment, not just a plot summary.
review.appeal: +5 — it has a hook (the witty opening line about sex scenes and food), but it is about a film review, which is less universally compelling than a topic like health or money.

zh.thesis: 新片《Tony》把布尔丹的感官世界拍成了平淡无奇的青春成长故事，完全没有把握住他的精神。
paragraphs: 《厨房机密》是本黑幽默又充满欲望的书。布尔丹写第一次吃牡蛎，说它是「闪亮的、隐约带着性意味的东西，还在滴水，几乎活着」。他自称享乐主义者，对体验如饥似渴。
但导演 Matt Johnson 的《Tony》不是关于布尔丹的胃口。它讲的是一个讨厌的中产少年，1975 年夏天在普罗温斯敦追女孩，被迫去海鲜店洗锅，跟着主厨学规矩，爱上那帮海盗般的同事。
电影里只有 1.5 场性爱戏，食物看起来「还行」——两个问题。布尔丹那标志性的好奇心、性感和待人接物的本事，全被刻意淡化了。
名人起源故事本来就难拍：得在成名前种下日后人格的种子。但这部片把焦点收得太窄，回避了布尔丹一生的广度和复杂度，只剩一个谁都可能经历过的夏天。
所以真正的问题不是电影好不好看，而是它把布尔丹拍成了普通人。这恰恰丢掉了让他成为布尔丹的东西。

en.thesis: The new film 'Tony' turns Bourdain's sensual world into a bland coming-of-age story, missing his spirit entirely.
paragraphs: 'Kitchen Confidential' is a darkly funny, lusty book. Bourdain writes of his first oyster as a 'glistening, vaguely sexual-looking object, still dripping and nearly alive'. He calls himself a sensualist, hungry for experience.

But Matt Johnson's 'Tony' is not about Bourdain's appetite. It follows an obnoxious middle-class teen, summer 1975 in Provincetown, chasing a girl, forced to wash pots at a seafood shack, learning discipline from the head chef, and falling for the pirate crew he works with.
There are only 1.5 sex scenes and the food looks 'just fine' — two of its problems. Bourdain's signature curiosity, sexuality, and way with people are deliberately underplayed.

Origin stories are tricky: they must plant seeds of a persona before it forms. But this film narrows its focus so much that it sidesteps the breadth, drama, and complexity of Bourdain's life, leaving a summer that could belong to anyone.
So the real problem isn't whether the film is good, but that it makes Bourdain ordinary — which is exactly what loses what made him Bourdain.

articles.title: The Wonders of the Male Human Pelvis
articles.titleZh: 男性人类骨盆的奇妙之处
articles.author: Jake Currie

review.argument: Argument: it claims the male human pelvis has a unique forward-oriented hip socket configuration that improves walking efficiency, and contrasts it with the female pelvis constrained by childbirth. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how evolutionary trade-offs shape bodies differently, and the reader can apply it to thinking about sex differences and adaptation. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the study summary.
review.appeal: +8 — it is about the reader's own body, has a hook (male pelvis overlooked), and is readable cold, though it lacks scenes or people.

zh.thesis: 男性骨盆独特的结构是一种为了高效行走的进化适应，而女性骨盆因分娩需求无法发展出这种结构。
paragraphs: 关于女性骨盆的研究很多，因为「产科困境」——人类分娩比其他哺乳动物更困难——涉及许多进化权衡问题。男性骨盆相对被忽视了，直到现在。
一项发表在《Scientific Reports》上的新研究分析了 91 个现代人类骨盆和两个男性尼安德特人骨盆，发现现代男性骨盆的髋臼更朝前，这种独有结构有益于行走。
行走被描述为一系列「受控的跌落」：身体重心失衡，再迈腿接住自己。这个过程中身体下降，既给关节压力，也要耗能恢复。
男性骨盆的结构让股四头肌既能吸收冲击，又能把身体弹回，步态更省力，这可能让男性在长距离行走上有优势。女性骨盆因分娩需求无法发展出这些改造。
这些发现的应用不止于进化研究。研究者说，理解行走机制的演化，有助于当代生物力学、肌肉骨骼医学、康复和损伤预防的研究，尼安德特人的视角帮我们更懂现代人体。

en.thesis: The unique architecture of the male human pelvis is an adaptation for efficient walking, one women's pelvises couldn't develop because of childbirth demands.
paragraphs: There is plenty of research on the female pelvis, for good reason. The so-called 'obstetrical dilemma' — why human childbirth is so hard compared to other mammals — involves many evolutionary trade-offs. The male pelvis has been relatively overlooked, until now.

A new study in Scientific Reports analyzed 91 modern human pelvises and two male Neanderthal pelvises. It found the modern male pelvis is unique, with hip sockets oriented more toward the front, an adaptation that benefits locomotion.

Walking has been described as a series of controlled falls: you destabilize your center of gravity, then swing a leg forward to catch yourself. Each fall drops your body down, stressing joints and costing energy to recover.

The male pelvis's architecture lets the quads both absorb the shock of stepping and spring the body back up, making the gait more energy efficient. This may give men an advantage over long distances. Women's pelvises couldn't develop these modifications, being constrained by childbirth.

The findings reach beyond evolution. Understanding our walking mechanism, the researchers say, can inform biomechanics, musculoskeletal medicine, rehabilitation and injury prevention research, and the Neanderthal perspective helps us better understand the modern human body.

articles.title: 我错过了多少泼天的富贵？

review.argument: Argument: it claims that missing investment gains is due to delayed cognition, and caps it with the aphorism that one cannot earn or keep money beyond one's awareness. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how personal regret over missed opportunities is framed as a cognitive limitation, and the reader can apply this to any field where timing matters. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that cognition, not fate, determines financial success, which is challenged in the comments.
review.appeal: +5 — it is about personal finance, a topic people live with, and the hook of 'missed riches' is relatable, but the piece is thin and mostly a prompt for comments.

zh.thesis: 认知晚了几年，就错过了半导体基金几百个点的涨幅。
paragraphs: 硅谷居士是个计算机博士，在硅谷做软件。他今天在博客上感慨，自己到2025年秋天，才意识到AI时代真的来了，而黄仁勋三年前就看到了。
他从2022年开始重仓半导体基金SMH，过去五年这只基金涨了363%。认知晚了这几年，泼天的富贵就错过了。
有同事问他，英伟达帮客户融资买自己的GPU，左脚踩右脚，是不是到了新高度。他说，黄仁勋和华尔街大佬肯定比我们聪明，他们不担心，我们也不用杞人忧天。
他觉得人挣不到认知以外的钱，也守不住认知以外的财富。留言区里有人感慨，早知三日事，多买一顷田；还有人后悔被投资行职员劝住，错过了标普500从498涨到768那波。
但也有读者说，自己的命运是被这位博主改写的——以前只敢碰A股，后来跟着他定投美股指数，现在账户涨了30%到90%。所以这篇既是感慨，也是劝大家别羡慕，认知到位了，机会还在。

en.thesis: A cognitive lag of a few years cost the author the massive gains of the semiconductor fund.
paragraphs: The author, a computer science PhD working on software in Silicon Valley, writes on his blog that he only realized in the fall of 2025 that the AI era had truly arrived, while Jensen Huang had seen it three years earlier.
He started heavily investing in the semiconductor fund SMH in 2022, which rose 363% over the past five years. That few years of cognitive lag cost him the windfall.

A colleague asked him about Nvidia helping customers finance their GPU purchases, calling it 'left foot stepping on right foot.' He replied that Jensen and Wall Street bigwigs are surely smarter, and if they aren't worried, we shouldn't borrow trouble.

He believes you can't earn money beyond your cognition, nor hold wealth beyond it. In the comments, some lamented 'knowing three days ahead, you'd buy an acre more of land'; another regretted being talked out of buying by a brokerage clerk and missing the S&P 500's run from 498 to 768.

But a reader said his destiny was rewritten by this blogger: having only dared to trade A-shares, he now follows the blogger's dollar-cost averaging into US index funds, and his account is up 30% to 90%. So the piece is both lament and encouragement: don't envy, get your cognition right, and opportunities remain.

rejected.title: The Best Ocean Photos of the Year

review.argument: Announcement: it reports the finalists of the Ocean Photographer of the Year 2026 awards and describes a selection of the images, with no contestable claim or argument beyond the contest's own promotional framing.
review.transfer: A non-specialist comes away with a glimpse of beautiful ocean photography and a few facts about marine life, but the piece is essentially a curated gallery; the transfer is minimal—it does not change how one thinks about the ocean or photography.
review.claim: A list: the writer selects and describes photos, but delete the writer and you lose only the curation and captions; there is no independent judgment or analysis that would be missed.
review.appeal: +5 — the images are inherently appealing and some facts (like the pygmy seahorse's size) are surprising, but the piece is passive viewing, not something a reader would urgently share.

rejected.title: Announcing Lenny’s Jobs: The best place in the world to find, vet, and land your dream job

review.argument: Announcement: it launches a job board with a list of features, and caps with a claim that it is the best place for four tech roles.
review.transfer: Non-specialist comes away with nothing transferable — it is a product launch for a niche audience, and the mechanism (vetting, AI tools) stays inside the job-search field.
review.claim: A list: the writer supplies selection and features, not a contestable claim; delete the writer and you lose the announcement, not an argument.
review.appeal: +0 — it is a product launch with no hook for an ordinary person, and the only people it interests are already in tech job hunting.

rejected.title: I tested Grok Bot, Grok 4.6, and Cursor Origin - here’s my honest take

review.argument: Announcement: it reports that the author tested Grok Bot, Cursor Origin, and Grok 4.6, and lists what she learned, but the body is a table of contents and timestamps, not an argument.
review.transfer: Nothing transfers — the takeaways are product-specific impressions ('multi-account connectors are the killer feature') that only matter to someone choosing among these tools; a generalist gains no portable mechanism.
review.claim: A list: the piece is a podcast episode summary with timestamps and links; delete the writer and you lose only the selection of topics, not a contestable claim.
review.appeal: +0 — no hook for an outsider, no scene, no contradiction of an assumption; it is a roundup for people already following the AI tool space.
